subtopic: Speculative decoding / Acceptance rate and speedup
learningObjective: Reason about how acceptance rate determines speedup in speculative decoding and where speedup is bounded.
stem: In a spec-decoded run with k = 5 proposals per step, the observed acceptance rate per proposed token is p = 0.7. The target forward costs ~10 ms; the draft forward costs ~2 ms per token. Which statement about expected speedup is correct?
profileData:
Setup:
  Target forward on k+1 positions:   10 ms
  Draft forward per token:            2 ms
  Proposals per verification:         k = 5
  Per-token acceptance probability:   p = 0.7 (independent Bernoulli approximation)

Expected accepted prefix length ≈ (1 - p^{k+1}) / (1 - p) for Bernoulli-independent acceptance.
  = (1 - 0.7^6) / 0.3 ≈ (1 - 0.117) / 0.3 ≈ 2.94 tokens
  Per-verification: 1 target step (10 ms) + 5 draft steps (5 * 2 = 10 ms) = 20 ms
  Expected accepted tokens per verification: ~2.94 + 1 (target's sample) = ~3.94
  Baseline: target alone = 10 ms per token

options.text: Speedup equals 1 / (1 - p) = 3.33x independent of k, because acceptance rate solely determines throughput; increasing k beyond 1 has no effect on wall time.
Speedup is exactly k = 5x because k tokens are proposed per target forward; the acceptance rate p only affects quality, not throughput.

Expected tokens per verification is ~3.94, at 20 ms per verification: ~0.20 tokens/ms. Baseline is 0.10 tokens/ms. Speedup ≈ 2x. Acceptance rate p is the dominant lever; as p → 1 speedup approaches (k+1) / (1 + draft-cost-fraction * (k+1)), bounded by the draft/target cost ratio.
Because the draft forward runs in parallel with the target forward on the same GPU, there is no draft overhead in wall time and speedup is (k+1) * p ≈ 4.2x.

explanation: With Bernoulli-independent acceptance, expected accepted prefix length is (1 - p^{k+1})/(1 - p) ≈ 2.94 tokens; the target also samples one output on rejection, giving ~3.94 tokens per verification. At 20 ms per verification (target + draft), that's 0.20 tokens/ms vs baseline 0.10 → ~2x speedup. As p → 1, speedup approaches the limit (k+1)/(1 + draft-cost-share), so both draft cost and k matter. A cheap draft (low cost) and high p push toward the asymptote.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: k does affect throughput; the formula ignores k.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: p < 1 shortens expected accepted prefix; k tokens are never guaranteed.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: right arithmetic and correct sensitivity analysis.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: draft cannot run in parallel with target on the same critical path; draft is sequential per step.

assumptions: Bernoulli-independent per-token acceptance is a first-order approximation; real acceptance is position-dependent.
Draft and target run on the same GPU without overlap; some implementations overlap by pipelining, complicating the calculus.
nonImplications: Does not imply Bernoulli independence holds exactly.
Does not imply k should always be increased; larger k raises variance and can hurt tail latency.

performanceClaim.scope: Expected speedup of speculative decoding as a function of k, p, and draft cost
